items.item_text: Graduation from an accredited college or university with a bachelor’s degree in accounting, finance, business administration or a related field.
Interpret, explain and apply complex legal mandates, regulations, guidelines, policies and procedures applicable to assigned responsibilities with consistency and a high degree of accuracy.
At least five (5) years of professional experience in accounting or budgeting, of which two (2) years were in a management or supervisory role.
Experience with a California community college, K-12 or other governmental fiscal environment.

A District on-line application on http://hr.fhda.edu/careers/ . *In the application, you will provide information, which demonstrates your understanding of, sensitivity to, and respect for the diverse academic, socio-economic, ethnic, religious, and cultural backgrounds, disability, and sexual orientation of community college students, faculty and staff. Additionally, you will be asked to explain how your life experiences, studies or work have influenced your commitment to diversity, equity and inclusion.
A current resume of all work experience, formal education and training.
CPA Preferred

Principles, practices and procedures of general and governmental accounting and applic­able sections of Generally Accepted Accounting Prin­ciples (GAAP), Financial Accounting Standards Board (FASB) and Budget and Accounting Manual for Cali­fornia Community Colleges.
Management of accounting and financial operations including the review, maintenance and adjustment of funds, accounts and budgets to produce accurate financial and statistical records.
Preparation of financial statements and related comprehensive reports.
Local, state, and federal laws pertaining to applicable sections of the California State Education Code and Title 5.
Uses and operations of financial modules of ERP.
Board Policies, Administrative Procedures, Human Resources policies and procedures, Equal Employment Opportunity, and collective bargaining agreements.
Understanding and implementation of shared governance, teambuilding, and collaborative decision-making processes within and across division/department lines.
Organize, plan and manage the staff, operations, and activities of Districtwide accounting section.

Manage, reconcile and analyze complex financial and statistical data and prepare financial analyses and reports, sum­mary conclusions, and recommendations in accordance with GAAP, GASB, FASB and various funder and legal requirements.
Select, motivate, and evaluate staff and provide for their training and professional develop­ment.
Prepare clear, concise and comprehensive correspondence, financial and grant state­ments, reports, and other written materials.
Research and evaluate information and data used in informed financial decision making and reporting.
Participate in complex financial and grant-related audits.
Demonstrate improvement in process efficiency, service delivery, cross-department collaboration, and technical innovation.
Advance and use current and emerging technology including office equipment, computers, and specialized software programs including complex integrated financial systems
Establish, maintain, and foster positive and effective working relationships with those contacted in the course of work.
A cover letter addressing your qualifications for the position.

Understanding of, sensitivity to, and respect for the diverse academic, socio-economic, ethnic, religious, and cultural backgrounds, disability, and sexual orientation of community college students, faculty and staff.
Communicate and present information effectively both orally and in writing to a variety of audiences.
